name: Autonomous Swarm Dispersal Unit ASDU-4 'Locust'
description:
The ASDU-4 is a mid-chassis autonomous swarm drone housing a colony of 200–400 micro-units, each roughly the size of a thumbnail, fabricated from carbon-composite shells and equipped with independent piezoelectric propulsion fins. Upon deployment, the colony disperses in configurable patterns—cordon, pursuit, saturation, or denial—governed by a distributed hive-logic processor that eliminates the need for a centralized command node. Each micro-unit carries a 0.8-gram shaped charge of TATP-analog high explosive capable of penetrating soft armor at contact range, delivering lethal fragmentation to unarmored targets and sustained harassment to hardened ones.

What distinguishes the ASDU-4 from earlier swarm prototypes is its fault-tolerant mesh communication architecture. Destroying individual units does not degrade swarm cohesion; the colony reorganizes and redistributes targeting priorities in under 40 milliseconds. The swarm can navigate urban geometry autonomously using onboard LIDAR pings shared across the mesh, threading corridors, ventilation ducts, and vehicle interiors that conventional weapons cannot reach. A proprietary IFF beacon system—licensed separately—prevents friendly casualties, though bootleg units circulating in the GLMZ undermarket frequently lack this feature entirely.

Operators in the field refer to deployment as 'opening the box,' and the psychological impact on targeted personnel is disproportionate to the ASDU-4's raw lethality. The sound of the swarm—a low, chittering harmonic produced by thousands of synchronized propulsion fins—has become a recognizable signature in contested districts. Several documented cases exist of entire security teams abandoning fortified positions upon auditory detection alone.
legality: Prohibited — classified as area-denial swarm munition under Meridian Autonomous Weapons Accord, Article 9
specifications: colony count: 200–400 units (standard loadout) unit dimensions: 22mm x 14mm x 8mm unit mass: 3.1 grams each payload per unit: 0.8g TATP-analog contact charge operational range: Up to 600 meters from deployment point battery life: 18 minutes sustained flight swarm reorganization latency: 38–42ms deployment chassis: 310mm x 210mm x 90mm hardcase canister IFF compatibility: Arcturus Beacon Protocol v4 (optional module, sold separately) environmental limits: Degraded performance above wind speeds of 35 km/h; waterproof to 1m submersion
tactical_use: Deployed primarily for area denial, room clearing, and pursuit of fleeing targets through complex terrain. Corporate extraction teams use cordon-pattern deployment to collapse escape routes before breaching. Street operators favor saturation patterns for ambush scenarios in tight corridors. The swarm's autonomous navigation removes the operator from direct line of sight, making it attractive for remote activation traps. Counter-swarm protocols involve high-frequency sonic disruptors or EMP bursts, both of which require dedicated equipment rarely carried by civilian security.
cultural_context: The ASDU-4 occupies a particular place of dread in GLMZ's street mythology. Unlike a bullet or a blade, the swarm feels alive—purposeful in a way that unsettles even hardened operators. In the Kowloon Stack and the Sublevel markets, possession of a Locust Box is a credibility marker among fixers and mid-tier enforcers, though using one in a civilian district carries severe social consequences within most criminal organizations. Corporate sec-teams deploying ASDU-4 units in residential zones during the Vertical 9 Evictions of 2197 permanently damaged public perception of ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS, a PR wound the company has not fully recovered from.
known_users: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS black-site extraction teams
Ghost-market fixers specializing in contested-zone operations
GLMZ PD Counter-Terrorism Unit (licensed, restricted deployment)
story_hooks: A bootleg ASDU-4 without IFF beacons has been traced to a series of killings in a residential stack—but the swarm's hive-log, if recovered, contains targeting data that implicates a corporate client, not a street operator.
A fixer is hired to retrieve an ASDU-4 canister abandoned in a sealed sublevel after a botched operation. The swarm inside is still active, still patrolling, and has been doing so for three weeks.

An ARCTURUS whistleblower claims the IFF beacon protocol has a backdoor allowing the manufacturer to override friendly-fire protection remotely. She needs an escort to the press and someone is already hunting her.

A player character wakes up with an ASDU-4 deployment canister chained to their wrist and a timer counting down. Someone wants something delivered—or wants them to figure out why they were chosen as the delivery mechanism.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, utilitarian hardcase canister resembling a flattened ammunition box or tactical munitions container. The exterior presents a deliberately sterile, industrial appearance—no chrome, no aggressive aesthetics. At rest, it is inert and unremarkable; only the faint geometric scarring on the lid hints at internal complexity.
physical_description.dimensions: 310mm length × 210mm width × 90mm height (deployment chassis); individual micro-units measure 22mm × 14mm × 8mm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light for its footprint—the canister feels almost insubstantial when held, creating cognitive dissonance with its lethality. The micro-units themselves are negligible in hand; the colony's mass is distributed across hundreds of bodies rather than concentrated in a single frame.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-composite shell for micro-units; deployment canister fabricated from reinforced polymer with internal titanium latch fixtures
physical_description.finish: Matte battleship gray with subtle texture to reduce glare and fingerprints. Micro-unit shells exhibit a faint iridescent sheen under direct light—a byproduct of carbon-composite layering—creating an almost organic luster.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with matte black interior padding visible through venting apertures. Accent striping in industrial orange marks power-state indicators and IFF module sockets (when present).
physical_description.grip_texture: Deployment canister features recessed grip wells molded into polymer—designed for gloved hands, slightly tacky rubberized coating. Individual micro-units are smooth, almost slick to the touch, with barely perceptible ribbing where propulsion fins articulate.
distinctive_features: Hinged lid with three-point pressure-release latches that emit a sharp *clack* when disengaged
Faint LED aperture (orange when armed, dark when dormant) recessed into canister corner
Internal mesh of dimpled foam padding engineered to suppress vibration during transport
Hairline gaps between micro-unit clusters visible only under magnification—evidence of the hive-logic segregation architecture
Piezoelectric fin ribbing on each micro-unit catches light in subtle striations, creating a 'scaled' appearance in mass
IFF module socket (rectangular, keyed) on canister flank—often empty on bootleg units, leaving an obvious void
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Ironside Armaments corporate seal—a stylized iron fist clasping a circuit node—embossed (not stamped) on canister lid. Serial number laser-etched in 4mm type below seal. Production date cipher molded into rear panel. Warning text in Meridian Standard: 'AUTONOMOUS MUNITION — HAZARDOUS — PROHIBITED UNDER MAWC ART. 9' in 2mm white stencil.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show accelerated wear: scuffed polymer, scratched lid, occasional denting at corners from transport in tactical gear. Electronics remain pristine—the active components are sealed and shielded. Battle-deployed units often display burn scoring on the lid from piezoelectric discharge residue. Bootleg variants exhibit crude modifications: hand-scratched serial numbers, missing IFF sockets, jury-rigged power switches.
